full_judgment: 4. The defendant Nos. 1-3 contested the suit by filing a written statement wherein the plaint case has been denied. The specific defence case is that Ismail and others and predecessors of these defendants took settlement of the suit land through a kabuliyat dated 30th Aswin, 1325 B.S. that thereafter the entire land covered by kabuliyat was partitioned and suit land fell in the saham of Ismail the predecessor of these defendants. Ismail died leaving four daughters Godar, Gedi, Ayiul and Sayful and maternal cousin Ain Ullah to inherit his properties. On an amicable partition amongst the heirs of Ismail the suit land fell in the saham of Ain Ullah alone. After the death of Ain Ullah the suit land has been correctly recorded in the name of his son Mazumder Ali. While Mazumder Ali was in possession of the suit land, he died leaving these defendants as his heirs to inherit and these defendants since then as heirs enjoyed the suit land by paying rents and taxes to the Government. The suit is not maintainable as it does not included the entire lands of the kabuliyat in the hutch pot. The record of the suit land has been correctly prepared and published. The suit having been instituted long after the preparation of settlement record the plaintiffs are not entitled to any relief and the suit is liable to be dismissed.
